guide.title: Dvořák: String Quartet No. 12, Op. 96 – IV. Finale (Vivace ma non troppo)
guide.overview: This finale is in F major and in a quick 2/4 beat. It has two big parts. Part 1 runs from [m. 1] to [m. 218]. A second part marked "Tempo I." runs from [m. 219] to the end at [m. 382]. Keys and chords here are estimated by computer, so treat them as a guide. Listen for the main tune, for the many key changes, and for the final climb to a very loud ending.

listening_points.headline: A soft, quiet opening
listening_points.text: The movement starts softly in F major. The second violin probably leads at first, with the others in step. The cello takes over briefly at [m. 4].

listening_points.headline: The first violin takes the tune
listening_points.text: The first violin leads from [m. 5], in F major. The tune it plays is the one to remember. It repeats at the same pitch at [m. 9-11]. The computer labels the key there D minor, but the tune itself is unchanged. Both times it is soft.

listening_points.headline: Back to F major, growing louder
listening_points.text: The key returns to F major at [m. 14]. The music swells from soft toward louder, because crescendo marks appear. By [m. 21] it is loud, with sharp accents.

listening_points.headline: Hushed passage, mostly soft
listening_points.text: The mood drops to soft at [m. 25]. The second violin probably leads here, though the lead is uncertain. At [m. 33] it falls to very soft. The first violin leads again there.

listening_points.headline: A darker A minor burst
listening_points.text: The key moves to A minor at [m. 42]. The music builds with crescendos. Then it suddenly becomes very loud at [m. 47-48]. It drops back to soft by [m. 49].

listening_points.headline: Bright C major build to a loud peak
listening_points.text: A brighter C major arrives at [m. 61]. The music grows louder, with a crescendo marked. It reaches very loud at [m. 65-66].

listening_points.headline: A long, quiet wandering through new keys
listening_points.text: After the loud peak, the music turns very soft. The key shifts through A-flat major, C minor, E-flat major, and back to A-flat major. The first violin mostly carries the tune. Dynamics stay mostly very soft, with a brief louder moment around [m. 94-98].

listening_points.headline: The viola steps forward
listening_points.text: At [m. 107-110] the viola leads, with high confidence in the analysis. Two parts play together as a duet. The key is B-flat minor. Then the first violin takes the lead again in F minor and C minor.

listening_points.headline: Loud, then everyone in octaves
listening_points.text: After crescendo marks at [m. 112-113], the music is loud at [m. 115]. The viola probably leads, but this is uncertain. At [m. 120-122] the parts play the same notes in octaves, and it fades to soft.

listening_points.headline: Rising energy to a very loud stretch
listening_points.text: At [m. 138] the music gets loud, and the lines move independently of each other. At [m. 146] it is very loud. Then at [m. 147-150] the parts play in octaves, and the key slides to D-flat major.

listening_points.headline: Fading into a hushed D-flat major
listening_points.text: The loud music fades with a diminuendo, meaning it gets softer gradually. At [m. 153] it is soft, and by [m. 155] very soft. The first violin plays alone at [m. 156]. Later the key moves to C minor and back to F major at [m. 168].

listening_points.headline: A long A minor stretch that fades away
listening_points.text: The key settles in A minor for the rest of Part 1. The first violin plays alone at [m. 178]. The second violin plays alone at [m. 198]. Many lines move independently near the end. The part closes very softly.

listening_points.headline: Section 2 begins, with a rise to loud
listening_points.text: The second section starts at [m. 219], marked Tempo I. The key is E major, then A minor, E minor and G major. The volume rises from soft to loud, and by [m. 233] it is very loud. The first violin leads.

listening_points.headline: Loud F major, then a cello solo
listening_points.text: At [m. 234] the key is F major and the music is very loud. At [m. 243] the key is A minor. The volume falls to medium loud at [m. 245], then climbs to loud. The cello plays alone at [m. 251].

listening_points.headline: A sudden, very hushed D-flat major
listening_points.text: At [m. 252] the music drops suddenly to extremely soft. The key is D-flat major. The first violin leads. From [m. 263] the music moves through several keys with crescendos building up.

listening_points.headline: Back to F major, with many soft and loud turns
listening_points.text: At [m. 275] the key is F major and the music is loud. It then softens. There are several short solo moments from [m. 281] on. Around [m. 314] the key turns to F minor, and at [m. 321] the music is very loud in F major.

listening_points.headline: The final push to a very loud ending
listening_points.text: From [m. 337] the key is F major, and it is mostly very loud. At [m. 371] the marking rises to fff, the loudest marking in the movement. A computer estimate marks [m. 378] as the loudest and busiest point. The parts play in octaves there. After a short turn to F minor [m. 369-374], the movement ends in F major.

glossary.explanation: The home note and scale of the music. Major keys sound brighter. Minor keys sound darker.
Several instruments playing the same notes at different heights.
All parts move together, in the same rhythm, like chords.
A mark meaning 'return to the first speed'.
